key_insight: A deep-learning surrogate can predict CFD-derived hemodynamic markers from patient-specific aneurysm geometry in real time, enabling rapid biomechanical assessment of non-idealized intracranial aneurysms.
problem_solved: CFD-based hemodynamic analysis is accurate but slow, requires specialized expertise, and is impractical for large-scale clinical use; the paper replaces slow simulations with a fast, automated surrogate suitable for real-world (non-idealized) patient geometries.
method: Train a deep surrogate model to map 3D aneurysm morphology (patient-specific geometries) to key biomechanical outputs previously obtained by CFD (e.g., wall shear stress, velocity fields, oscillatory indices).
Use a dataset of CFD simulations on non-idealized aneurysm geometries for supervised learning and validate surrogate predictions against high-fidelity CFD results.
Optimize model for real-time inference and clinically usable outputs (fast runtime, comparable spatial accuracy, and robustness to realistic boundary conditions).
impact: Enables scalable, rapid hemodynamic assessment for clinical trials and decision support, lowering the barrier to integrating biomechanics into patient care; relevant to ML practitioners building physics surrogates or clinical AI pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: patient imaging → geometry extraction → surrogate model → hemodynamic maps (real-time)
Side-by-side heatmap comparison of surrogate vs. CFD (e.g., WSS) on the same aneurysm surface
Scatter/box plot of accuracy vs. runtime showing surrogate speedup and error distribution relative to CFD
Iconic timeline or dashboard mockup showing 'minutes vs. hours' clinical workflow improvement
paper_title: RHSIA: Real-time Hemodynamics Surrogation for Non-idealized Intracranial Aneurysms
paper_authors: Yiying Sheng, Wenhao Ding, Dylan Roi, Leonard Leong Litt Yeo, Hwa Liang Leo
